title: A Look Is Not a Cause

scenes.tts: This cell tore open. What killed it: an accident, or a program? Chapter one showed two endings: an apoptotic cell held its membrane until eaten; a necrotic cell tore early.
scenes.narration: This cell tore open. What killed it: an accident, or a program? Chapter one showed two endings: an apoptotic cell held its membrane until eaten; a necrotic cell tore early.
scenes.caption: This cell tore open. What killed it: an accident, or a program? Chapter one showed two endings: an apoptotic cell held its membrane until eaten; a necrotic cell tore early.
scenes.visual: COLOUR MAP, carried from chapter 1 (one colour per concept): BLUE = the plasma membrane, a thick ring; TEAL = caspases, small scissor cartoons; YELLOW = phosphatidylserine, small round lipid heads; GREEN = the phagocyte; RED = spilled contents and alarm signals; GREY = nucleus, outlines, other cells and machinery blocks; new in chapter 2: PURPLE = annexin V, small curved clips; ORANGE = propidium iodide, small orange dots. Labels in white or the concept colour, size 28 or larger. HOOK, no title first. Open on a torn cell that fills about 70% of frame height, with RED contents seeping slowly across the floor. On 'What killed it', a white question card appears at the top: 'What killed it?'. On 'an accident, or a program?', two white tags drift in on either side of the cell: 'accident?' and 'program?'; both pulse gently. On 'Chapter one showed two endings', the cell shrinks to the lower right and chapter 1's closing pair settles across the bottom: left, a shrunken BLUE-ringed cell inside a GREEN phagocyte, labelled 'sealed and eaten'; right, the torn cell, labelled 'torn early'.
Title 'A Look Is Not a Cause' fades in at the top for 2 s over the torn cell, whose RED spill keeps creeping slowly outward. The two tags fade out.

scenes.tts: For decades, these two looks were taught as a pair. Apoptosis, named in nineteen seventy-two by Kerr, Wyllie and Currie, was the programmed death. Necrosis was the accident. That pairing has not survived.
scenes.narration: For decades, these two looks were taught as a pair. Apoptosis, named in 1972 by Kerr, Wyllie and Currie, was the programmed death. Necrosis was the accident. That pairing has not survived.
scenes.caption: For decades, these two looks were taught as a pair. Apoptosis, named in 1972 by Kerr, Wyllie and Currie, was the programmed death. Necrosis was the accident. That pairing has not survived.
scenes.visual: The torn cell slides to the right half of the frame; the shrunken, BLUE-ringed apoptotic cell from chapter 1 (with TEAL scissors inside and two small blebs) slides in on the left, both at full size. A white bracket joins them from above, labelled 'taught as a pair'. On '1972', a small white tag '1972: Kerr, Wyllie, Currie' appears above the left cell, then the label 'apoptosis: programmed' writes on under it. On 'the accident', 'necrosis: accident' writes on under the right cell. On 'has not survived', the word 'accident' under the right cell is struck through with a white line and fades out; the bracket breaks in the middle.

scenes.tts: A regulated death runs on dedicated machinery. Genes or drugs can turn that machinery up or down. Such a cell can still look necrotic. Three such deaths are defined by what they depend on.
scenes.narration: A regulated death runs on dedicated machinery. Genes or drugs can turn that machinery up or down. Such a cell can still look necrotic. Three such deaths are defined by what they depend on.
scenes.caption: A regulated death runs on dedicated machinery. Genes or drugs can turn that machinery up or down. Such a cell can still look necrotic. Three such deaths are defined by what they depend on.
scenes.visual: The apoptotic cell fades; the torn cell moves back to centre, but now shown intact and about to die (BLUE ring whole, GREY nucleus). Show, then name: inside it, a small GREY machinery block (unlabelled) appears, with a white dial beside it. A small white chip labelled 'gene change' and a small white pill cartoon each turn the dial up, then down; the block brightens and dims with it. Label 'regulated: dedicated machinery' in white appears after the dial has moved twice. On 'still look necrotic', the cell swells to about 1.4 times its size and its BLUE ring tears open, RED spilling, while the GREY block stays lit inside. On 'Three such deaths', the cell resets (whole again) and is copied into three cells in a row across the frame, each about 45% of frame height, labelled underneath only with 1, 2, 3.

scenes.tts: First, necroptosis. Activated R I P K three adds phosphate to M L K L. Clusters of M L K L then move to the plasma membrane.
scenes.narration: First, necroptosis. Activated RIPK3 adds phosphate to MLKL. Clusters of MLKL then move to the plasma membrane.
scenes.caption: First, necroptosis. Activated RIPK3 adds phosphate to MLKL. Clusters of MLKL then move to the plasma membrane.
scenes.visual: Camera moves onto cell 1 (left), which grows to fill about 65% of frame height. Two GREY labelled blocks inside: 'RIPK3' and 'MLKL'. Show, then name: a small white 'P' tag jumps from the RIPK3 block onto the MLKL block, which lights up white. Several MLKL blocks then gather into small clusters (schematic, plain rounded blocks, no structures) that drift outward and settle in the BLUE ring. The membrane is not shown opening here. Label 'necroptosis' appears in white above the cell after the clusters reach the ring; small tag beneath: 'mammalian model'.

scenes.tts: Second, pyroptosis. Gasdermins are cut, freeing fragments that form pores in the plasma membrane. It often, but not always, follows inflammatory caspases.
scenes.narration: Second, pyroptosis. Gasdermins are cut, freeing fragments that form pores in the plasma membrane. It often, but not always, follows inflammatory caspases.
scenes.caption: Second, pyroptosis. Gasdermins are cut, freeing fragments that form pores in the plasma membrane. It often, but not always, follows inflammatory caspases.
scenes.visual: Camera slides to cell 2 (centre), which grows to fill about 65% of frame height. Inside, GREY blocks labelled 'gasdermin'. A pair of TEAL scissors labelled 'inflammatory caspases', with a small white tag 'often, not always', snips each block into two pieces. One freed piece from each travels to the BLUE membrane band. Small gaps labelled 'pores' open through the band beside the pieces; this shows pore function schematically, not molecular structure. RED dots stream out through the gaps. Label 'pyroptosis' appears in white above the cell after the first pore opens.

scenes.tts: Third, ferroptosis, driven by severe, iron-dependent damage to membrane lipids. G P X four is the main guard, reducing damaging lipid hydroperoxides. In cultured cells, drugs that trap iron block it.
scenes.narration: Third, ferroptosis, driven by severe, iron-dependent damage to membrane lipids. GPX4 is the main guard, reducing damaging lipid hydroperoxides. In cultured cells, drugs that trap iron block it.
scenes.caption: Third, ferroptosis, driven by severe, iron-dependent damage to membrane lipids. GPX4 is the main guard, reducing damaging lipid hydroperoxides. In cultured cells, drugs that trap iron block it.
scenes.visual: Camera slides to cell 3 (right), which grows to fill about 65% of frame height. Zoom to an arc of its BLUE ring drawn as a band. Small white sparks, with a small GREY dot labelled 'iron' beside them, hop along the band, and wherever they land the band turns ragged and RED-edged (schematic); label 'lipid damage' in white. On 'reducing damaging lipid hydroperoxides', a GREY block labelled 'GPX4' changes small text badges from 'lipid hydroperoxide' to 'reduced lipid product'; no molecular structures are drawn. On 'drugs that trap iron', a small white cage closes around the iron dot; the sparks stop and the band stays BLUE. Label 'ferroptosis' in white above the cell; small tag 'cultured cells' beside the cage.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry. A death's look names an endpoint, not a cause. To find the cause, block the machinery and see whether the death changes.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry. A death's look names an endpoint, not a cause. To find the cause, block the machinery and see whether the death changes.
scenes.caption: Here is the idea to carry. A death's look names an endpoint, not a cause. To find the cause, block the machinery and see whether the death changes.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to all three cells in a row, now all swollen and torn with RED spills, looking alike; their names fade so they read as three identical torn cells. Across the top, in white, the idea writes itself on: 'Look = endpoint, not cause'. On 'block the machinery', a white 'blocked' bar slides across the RIPK3 block inside cell 1 only; cell 1 rewinds smoothly: its ring closes, the RED draws back in and it stays whole and round, while cells 2 and 3 stay torn. Label under cell 1 in white: 'death changed'. Schematic; no numbers.

scenes.tts: Now take dying cells in a dish, with no phagocyte. Two dyes read chapter one's two membrane events. Annexin V binds phosphatidylserine it can reach from outside. Propidium iodide, a DNA dye, is kept out by an intact membrane.
scenes.narration: Now take dying cells in a dish, with no phagocyte. Two dyes read chapter one's two membrane events. Annexin V binds phosphatidylserine it can reach from outside. Propidium iodide, a DNA dye, is kept out by an intact membrane.
scenes.caption: Now take dying cells in a dish, with no phagocyte. Two dyes read chapter one's two membrane events. Annexin V binds phosphatidylserine it can reach from outside. Propidium iodide, a DNA dye, is kept out by an intact membrane.
scenes.visual: The dish from chapter 1 returns: a flat GREY circle seen from above, filling the frame, no GREEN cell anywhere. In it sits a shrunken apoptotic cell, BLUE ring intact, YELLOW heads on its outer face. Show, then name: small PURPLE clips drift in and snap onto the YELLOW heads, outlining the cell in PURPLE; label 'annexin V: flag' in PURPLE. On 'Propidium iodide', small ORANGE dots drift around the cell and bounce off the intact BLUE ring; none get in. Label 'propidium iodide' in ORANGE beside them.

scenes.tts: A flow cytometer reads both colours on each cell and places it in one of four boxes. An apoptotic cell in a dish often becomes flagged while intact. After secondary necrosis, it is flagged and leaky. The boxes are staining states, not verdicts.
scenes.narration: A flow cytometer reads both colours on each cell and places it in one of four boxes. An apoptotic cell in a dish often becomes flagged while intact. After secondary necrosis, it is flagged and leaky. The boxes are staining states, not verdicts.
scenes.caption: A flow cytometer reads both colours on each cell and places it in one of four boxes. An apoptotic cell in a dish often becomes flagged while intact. After secondary necrosis, it is flagged and leaky. The boxes are staining states, not verdicts.
scenes.visual: The dish shrinks into the upper left corner. A 2 by 2 grid fills the rest of the frame (about 70% of frame height): horizontal axis 'PI (leak)' in ORANGE runs from negative at left to positive at right; vertical axis 'annexin V (flag)' in PURPLE runs from negative at bottom to positive at top. The four boxes have faint corner tags 'neither', 'flag only', 'flag + leak', 'leak only'. A small white dot (the apoptotic cell) leaves the dish and drops into the 'flag only' box (annexin positive, PI negative). On 'After secondary necrosis', a small white clock labelled 'time (schematic)' sweeps once; the BLUE ring on the dish cell opens, ORANGE dots pour in and its nucleus glows ORANGE; at the same moment the white dot slides across into the 'flag + leak' box. On 'staining states, not verdicts', a white label 'state, not verdict' appears across the grid. Do NOT place any other kind of cell in the grid (the text asks where a torn cell lands).

scenes.tts: Other markers each report one event. TUNEL labels free DNA ends, whatever broke them. Cleaved caspase three shows the protease switched on, not that it killed. LDH, a cytosol enzyme, leaks through a torn membrane.
scenes.narration: Other markers each report one event. TUNEL labels free DNA ends, whatever broke them. Cleaved caspase-3 shows the protease switched on, not that it killed. LDH, a cytosol enzyme, leaks through a torn membrane.
scenes.caption: Other markers each report one event. TUNEL labels free DNA ends, whatever broke them. Cleaved caspase-3 shows the protease switched on, not that it killed. LDH, a cytosol enzyme, leaks through a torn membrane.
scenes.visual: The grid slides away. Three cards line up across the frame, each with a small cartoon that moves as it is named. Card 1 'TUNEL': a GREY DNA line snaps into pieces and a white glow lights the free ends; two small icons beside it (a shrunken BLUE-ringed cell and a swollen torn cell) both get the glow. Card 2 'cleaved caspase-3': a TEAL scissor blinks on; beside it a white '?' over a still-round cell. Card 3 'LDH': small RED dots labelled 'LDH' stream out through a tear in a BLUE ring into a beaker labelled 'medium'. Each card's label appears after its cartoon has moved.

scenes.tts: So does LDH mean a cell died? Researchers removed N I N J one, a small plasma membrane protein, from mouse macrophages. Then they triggered death. Will LDH pour out?
scenes.narration: So does LDH mean a cell died? Researchers removed NINJ1, a small plasma membrane protein, from mouse macrophages. Then they triggered death. Will LDH pour out?
scenes.caption: So does LDH mean a cell died? Researchers removed NINJ1, a small plasma membrane protein, from mouse macrophages. Then they triggered death. Will LDH pour out?
scenes.visual: Cards 1 and 2 fade; card 3 grows into the main picture: a GREEN-outlined macrophage (mouse) with a BLUE ring and RED LDH dots inside, beside the empty beaker 'medium'. Show, then name: a small GREY block sitting in the BLUE ring is lifted out and set aside with a white cross over it; label 'NINJ1' in white on the removed block. On 'triggered death', a white lightning cartoon strikes the cell; a generic GREY death-machinery block lights and the cell's insides go dark grey. Do not imply that every tested death used caspase-3. On 'Will LDH pour out?', a white question card appears at the top: 'Will LDH pour out?', and the empty beaker glows faintly.

Thinking pause. The question card 'Will LDH pour out?' stays on screen. The dying macrophage breathes slowly (its BLUE ring pulses in radius); the RED LDH dots drift inside it; the beaker stays empty. Nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: Very little came out. The cells died, but they stayed swollen, like balloons that never popped. Death and the final tear are separate steps. So LDH measures the tear, not the death.
scenes.narration: Very little came out. The cells died, but they stayed swollen, like balloons that never popped. Death and the final tear are separate steps. So LDH measures the tear, not the death.
scenes.caption: Very little came out. The cells died, but they stayed swollen, like balloons that never popped. Death and the final tear are separate steps. So LDH measures the tear, not the death.
scenes.visual: The question card fades. The macrophage swells to about 1.4 times its size, round and taut like a balloon, and stays sealed: its BLUE ring stretches but does not tear. Only one or two RED dots reach the beaker as a schematic contrast; label 'little LDH' in RED. Label 'dead, still sealed' in white above the cell. On 'separate steps', a white two-step timeline (schematic, no numbers) slides in underneath: step 1 'death' (ticked), step 2 'final tear' (empty box, the NINJ1 block shown greyed beside it). On 'LDH measures the tear', a RED arrow from the beaker points to step 2 only.

scenes.tts: So back to the torn cell. Its look tells you how it ended, not what killed it. To find the killer, block each candidate mechanism and watch what changes.
scenes.narration: So back to the torn cell. Its look tells you how it ended, not what killed it. To find the killer, block each candidate mechanism and watch what changes.
scenes.caption: So back to the torn cell. Its look tells you how it ended, not what killed it. To find the killer, block each candidate mechanism and watch what changes.
scenes.visual: Smooth zoom back to the torn cell from the hook, centred, RED spill on the dish floor; the question card 'What killed it?' returns at the top. Around the cell, three small white tags appear one by one, each naming a candidate mechanism: 'RIPK3 + MLKL', 'gasdermin', 'iron-dependent lipid damage'. On 'block each candidate mechanism', a white 'blocked' bar slides across one tag; on 'watch what changes', the torn cell beside it rewinds toward round and sealed while the other two tags stay lit. The question card changes to 'Test it.'

Standard end card on the dark background: Hex waves above the centred take-home sentence from the narration, 'A death's look names an endpoint, not a cause.' Small line beneath in TEAL: 'biochemistrypedia.com'.
